cars.specification_market: German-market production RCZ R launched early 2014, per the December 2013 Peugeot release. The earlier 260-PS R Concept is excluded. Source explicitly gives 199 kW / 270 PS and 330 Nm from 1900 to 5500 rpm. Exact capacity and gearbox are withheld in this selected transcription. Photo shows the production RCZ R at Geneva 2014, not the Paris 2012 concept.
cars.summary: The RCZ R represents Peugeot Sport’s engineering-led road coupe: its highly developed small turbo engine, Torsen differential, dedicated suspension and four-piston brakes made a complete performance flagship rather than a styling edition.
cars.admission_reason: The RCZ R represents Peugeot Sport’s engineering-led road coupe: its highly developed small turbo engine, Torsen differential, dedicated suspension and four-piston brakes made a complete performance flagship rather than a styling edition.

cars.specification_market: Original European 1970 2670-cc, 170-DIN-PS road reference from Citroën’s own historical technical account. Later injection and 3.0-litre specifications are excluded. No 1971 rally tune or race performance is used. Undefined mass and gearbox remain unfilled. Photo represents a European enclosed-headlamp SM; its build year and installed engine are not authenticated.
cars.summary: The SM is a landmark French grand tourer combining Maserati six-cylinder power with hydropneumatic suspension, high-pressure disc brakes and advanced assisted steering, extending Citroën’s distinctive chassis engineering into a fast front-drive coupe.

cars.specification_market: Original 2017 continental-European Première Edition launch specification, March 7 press kit pages 2–4 and 8–9. Manufacturer directly states 185 kW / 252 PS and 320 Nm. The prose’s 1080-kg figure and technical table’s 1103-kg DIN figure differ; no mass is imported. Later 300-PS, R, GT4 and electric models are excluded. Photo identifies a 2018 UK Première Edition of the same generation, not authentication of a 2017 continental build.
cars.summary: The modern A110 revived Alpine as a road-sports-car maker through an aluminium mid-engine coupe, pairing compact dimensions and double-wishbone suspension with a deliberate emphasis on agility and low mass.
